content.purpose: Reconnects continents, planes, histories, communities, souls, and ecosystems divided by a world-scale rupture without pretending they remained unchanged.
content.practice: Every side controls present identity, old claims, refugees, ecology, disease, contradiction, and the right not to reconnect.
content.consequence: Forgotten relations and dangers return, new lives are displaced, and the repaired world gains immense correspondence visible beyond itself.
content.failure: Restoration resurrects the cause of severance, forces reunion, or makes one side the authoritative original.

content.purpose: Allows a civilisation facing cosmic extinction to cross one final folded horizon, abandoning an ending world without guaranteeing where, when, or as what it will arrive.
content.practice: Survivors, those who remain, other beings, memory, identity, destination life, dissent, and unknown futures hold independent vetoes.
content.consequence: The old world becomes unreachable, names and bodies change in transit, and arrival creates an unprecedented claim upon another reality.
content.failure: The horizon preserves empire, consumes those outside the chosen pattern, repeats endlessly, or restores an idealised past instead of permitting a future.

content.counterplay: Refuse departure, break either Aspect relation, preserve an untaken refuge, deny the common name, or let the old world end without crossing.
